segments: 414 The dynastic rules {OCR?}. And he conquered {OCR?} all the lands.
And there came to him from Edessa Qayṣar-Shāh, his brother,
who had fled from his brother Rukn al-Dīn when he took Melitene from him.
And Ghiyāth al-Dīn did not receive him to himself,
but gave him much gold,
and sent him back again to Edessa.
And when the Sultan Ghiyāth al-Dīn went to Caesarea,
there came to him al-Malik al-Afḍal, the son of Saladin, the lord of Samosata, and also Niẓām al-Dīn, the lord of Ḥiṣn Ziyād (Kharput);
and they became subject to him,
and he became very great.
And in that same year, Nāṣir al-Dīn Maḥmūd, the son of Muḥammad, the son of Qara Arslān, the lord of Amid, went to al-Malik al-Ashraf, the son of al-ʿĀdil,
and asked that he should go with him,
and take Ḥiṣn Ziyād for him according to his promise.
And when al-Ashraf had gathered the forces of Syria, Mosul, Sinjar, and the Jazīrah,
he marched against Ḥiṣn Ziyād.
And they took the city,
and began to wage war against the fortress.
Then the lord of Ḥiṣn Ziyād sent to Sultan Ghiyāth al-Dīn,
and asked for help.
And the Sultan sent him six thousand horsemen with al-Malik al-Afḍal, the lord of Samosata.
And when they reached Melitene,
al-Ashraf and the lord of Amid heard [of it],
and they turned away from Kharput {OCR?}.
And they went and encamped against the lake of Samānīn {OCR?},
in the midst of which are two fortresses,
one belonging to the lord of Amid,
and the other to the lord of Ḥiṣn Ziyād.
And they attacked the one belonging to the lord of the fortress,
and captured it and placed guards in it.
And when the Sultan's army arrived at Kharput,
the lord of Amid marched towards Amid,
and the Sultan's army returned to the land of the Romans.
And in this year,
which is the year 1516
of the Greeks
(1205 of our Lord?):
the Iberians (Georgians) went out to the country of Adharbayjan,
and made a great slaughter,
and took vast spoil.
And from there they came to the country of Khilāṭ,
and caused great devastation.
And from there they came to the country of Arjīsh,
and plundered and burned,
and they went and encamped against the fortress between {OCR?} Khilāṭ and Erzurum.
Then the lord of Khilāṭ went to the son of Qilij Arslān, the lord of Erzurum,
and obtained forces from him.
And they came and encountered the Iberians,
and Zakaria the younger, the commander-in-chief of the Iberians, was killed in battle,
and the Iberians abandoned [the siege] and departed to their own country.
